chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
When you want to apply hanut to the deceased, then take camphor and wipe with it the marks of sajdah on him, all of his joints, his head, his beard, and place some of the hanut upon his chest.
And he said: The hanut for the man and the woman is the same.
And he said: I dislike that he be followed with a censer.

key_terms.آثَارَ السُّجُودِ: the bodily places associated with prostration
key_terms.الْحَنُوطُ: the perfuming substance applied to the deceased, especially camphor
key_terms.تُحَنِّطَ: to apply hanut to the deceased body

ai.seo_question: How should hanut be applied to the deceased according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the application of hanut to the deceased, specifying the use of camphor on the places of sajdah, the joints, the head, the beard, and the chest. It also states that the ruling is the same for men and women, and expresses disapproval of accompanying the deceased with a censer.
